## Chapter Thirteen

A New Day



Dawn broke over the old buildings and made its way through the small window of Lucas’s room. A light knock at the door signaled his time to get up and with a groan of aching muscles from the day before Lucas stood up from the bed, realizing he had never even taking off his shoes before passing out.

Coming out of the room, he looked left to see the open bathroom door as the smell of coffee permeated the open floorplan of the apartment. He stumbled into white tiled sanctuary finding a new set of folded clothes on the top of the toilet along with a bar of soap and took the hint with a smile. He clumsily disrobed and turned on the shower, He looked himself over in the mirror above the clam shell sink as he waited for the water to get hot. He could see the dark circles under his eyes and bruises and scratches from the woods hike the day before. With a shake of his head, he stepped into the scalding hot water, submerging his head.

Coming out of the bathroom in the clean pair of Jeans and the black t-shirt that was just tight enough to show off the definition of his chest courtesy of prison. He walked barefoot to the kitchen where Job was pouring coffee. “Good morning” he said sliding a cup to his young friend. “The clothes suit you” Lucas nodded and took a sip of the bitter black liquid. He savored the flavor having not had real coffee in years. “God, I missed this” he said breathlessly and took another eager sip. Job turned to the stove where the sound of bacon frying could be heard from the stove. “We have a busy day and I need you to come up to speed quickly, so I will be sending you on a few errands this afternoon, but first we need to get you setup with a new identity” he said, panning the bacon onto a plate with scrambled eggs and toast.

Lucas consumed the hearty breakfast with gusto and when he was done. Helped by cleaning the dishes while Job got ready for the morning. They left the shop and walked a block and came to stand in front of a large and surprisingly still intact building, it was mammoth covering the whole block. “This used to be the Marine Barracks a hundred or so years ago” Job said “It’s now basically apartments, but we are going beneath it.” He finished and continued to about halfway down the black to a non-descript set of stairs leading down. They both came to stand in front of a large iron door and Job knocked three times, he repeated it two more times before a groggy Asian man opened the small peephole in the door. Rubbing his eyes, he eyed the two critically “Nice red slippers, where did you get them?” he asked bored. Job rolled his eyes “Christ chow, it’s me” he said, the Asian man just stared at him without moving. With a dramatic sigh Job answered, “Not in Kansas Dorothy” and then with a nod the door slowly swung open with a groan and they entered into a cramped hall filled with pipes running deeper into the building. The Asian man waved his arm, and both followed down the hall. They walked a good half a block before coming to a set of stairs leading off the to the right and they entered it, descending down deeper into the bowels of the building. The hallway quickly opened onto a large concrete room, with hanging lights and a debris ridden dancefloor. Along one wall was a black wooden bar. The room obviously was not supposed to be seen in the light as the wood was worn and the floor was scuffed, it looked dirty and well used.

“Welcome to Studio DC” came a deep booming Boston accent from behind the bar. Lucas looked to see a large portly man with a woman’s grey wig and a pink Kimono, his large hands gently cradling a large steaming mug. Job smiled and descended the stairs “Lucas, I would like you to meet Aunt Sally” he said, coming to stand before the other man and throwing his arms around him. The man returned the warm hug with a smile. “Good to see you Job, was worried when I heard about the explosion in Frederick, do you know if our friend got out ok?” he asked with concern in his deep gravelly voice. Job shook his head “I don’t know, I was hoping you had heard from him” he answered. Sally sighed “Not yet “he said and then turned his attention to Lucas “And this is Dyson’s protégé” he said with a smile. Walking over and giving Lucas a bone crushing bear hug and a kiss on his check. Pushing him to arm’s length he smiled “Let this old queen get a look at you” Lucas couldn’t help but smile at the endearing nature of the older man. “It’s good to meet you Aunt Sally” he said still smiling. Looking around at the bar “What is this place” he asked curiously. Sally Stepped around from the bar looking up at the worn lighting and exposed wires hanging across the rafters. “Well since the government decreed fifty years ago that anyone who is not a good decent heterosexual fell under the new moral decency law, thus meaning if you are a queer, lesbian, tranny, cross dresser or other dangerous freak” he said sarcastically “Then you could go to jail for up to ten years for being yourself, This place lets us get together and be ourselves, without judgement or reprisals” he answered proudly. “The country may have gone to shit, but as long as there are places like this, that accept all people as they are for who they are then there is hope for a future” he finished. Cinching up his kimono he walked back to the two “But you didn’t come here to get a tour, what can I do for you?” he asked. Leaning on the bar and putting the coffee down.

Job pulled the packet out of his Jacket, Lucas recognized as the one he had gotten in Frederick “We have a new ID for Lucas, but I need to know if it’s still clean, after the incident in Frederick, I am afraid it’s been compromised” he said, handing the packet over.

With a booming voice Sally whispered to Chow who dutifully nodded and tehn walked back  through a swinging door. “Ill get it checked out, but I guess you aren’t just here for that” he said smiling and Job returned it nodded, I need an uptown packet and weapons” he finished. Sally nodded “getting the boy right into it, gotcha” he said reaching under the bar and pulling out a satchel. “This will get you out for a few hours, just drop off the package before you return” he said sliding the brown satchel towards Lucas. With a questioning look he glanced at Job who nodded, and he took it, putting the strap over his shoulder.

Sally smiled “So much to learn young one” he said his voice a dichotomy as it both sounded like a Boston construction worker and maternal as well. “Its easy to get into poor town dear, but next to impossible to get out, unless you are going to work or delivering something” he said “ergo, the bag, that is a delivery for a man who lives uptown, that will get you through the gate so you can complete the tasks Job has for you without raising suspicion” he answered. Lucas nodded, thinking he might understand. “Now” Sally started clapping his hands as he motioned for the two to join him and he too walked back into the back room of the club. He motioned for the two to wait in the kitchen while he proceeded into the back office. “You are going to pick up messages today” Job said, catching the young man off guard “What?” Lucas asked not understanding. Job turned to him leaning in “We can’t use electronic means of communication, we can’t send emails or messages , everything is watched, cataloged and tracked, so we use dead drops, places where messages are left , and we leave messages, this is how we communicate with various informants and cells” he said explaining his statement. Lucas understood, in prison he had read every book on early spy craft, war tactics, generals, philosophy, biology and much more. His mind was trained well he could have told Job that the dead drop or dead letter drop was used back in the days of the cold war allowing people to pass messages, packages or letters thus allowing them to maintain operational security by never actually meeting. Lucas nodded and they waited in silence for Sally to return. Which he did a moment later carrying a Black gym bag.  He gently laid it on the counter and turned to the two. “Did you explain to him why we don’t use guns?” he asked arching an eye at Job. The old man hung his head “I have explained a little, but please, I know you love listening to your own voice so regale us with your deep knowledge of all things weaponry” Job finished getting a mock irritated look from Sally.

“Flattery will get you everywhere, old man” he said flipping the hair back on his wig theatrically. Lucas smiled at the banter between the two old friends. “Unlike the British guns have been in the fabric of this country and the gun lobby even after the government takeover wielded incredible power. But the new government did not want to just hand out weapons to new citizens it had just staged a coup upon. So, they made did two things, and these two things allowed them full control over firearms nationwide.” Sally began and Lucas could tell he loved being the center of attention as he spun his tale. “They did two things, one they made it mandatory that all guns have grips that had dna recognition systems and that every gun and every barrel be registered with its shot pattern, also every grip and dna pattern had to be registered as well , meaning that if any gun is shot and any investigation could immediately confirm the gun and the person who fired it, making it next to impossible to kill someone anonymously with a firearms” he finished. Lucas raised his hand and quickly lowered it, feeling like an idiot, he wasn’t in class he thought, giving both men a sheepish grin. “You have a question?” Sally asked graciously. “Um yes, wouldn’t it be easy to get an older weapon or one from overseas which didn’t require a DNA pattern?” he asked, looking between both men to see if that might have been a stupid question. Neither scoffed and Job even nodded “Good question” he said and motioned to Sally to answer.

“That’s where the lovely Cerberus system comes into play, not only does it have audio and camera access, but there are sensors all over the city, that randomly scan and inventory people on the street, it would spot any gun either metal or polymer and instantly an officer would be dispatched to the location unless that person had a permit on file for that gun’s profile and Serial number, which is emitted by the grip wirelessly and can’t be spoofed” He finished leaning back content. Lucas shook his head. “Damn, I didn’t realize that” he said. “So, if they have sensors then they can detect any weapon carried on a person, so how do we get around that?” he asked, interested now in where this was going. Sally Smiled and with a theatrical motioned of his arms, unzipped the gym bag and laid out a rolled towel, he gently unrolled it revealing three and a half inch shiny black blades with the same color rubber handles. “Now If I know Dyson, you were trained in hand to hand and knife fighting” and Lucas remembered the hours and hours repeating cut and slash moves with the wooden five-inch stick, Dyson had him repeated them daily, weekly for a few years until the motions were second nature. He nodded looking curiously at the knifes laid out.  “The way we get around that is these are artificially grown obsidian blades, so they have no identifiable composition that the scanners recognize as weaponry, to them it probably looks the same as a bracelet with stones on it. These blades are razor sharp and very durable, also perfectly balanced.” He finished picking up the blade and expertly spinning it in his hand.

Lucas, with prodding from Sally, picked up one and weighed it in his hand, it was well balanced and fit well in his hand. Now his training in hand to hand and knives made more sense. He spun it again, reversing the grip on the blade and took a few practice jabs at the air. With a nod of approval, he handed the blade, hilt first back to Sally. “Sally, set us up with a six pack and a lower back harness” Job said and with a nod , Sally put the back away, Chow appearing and taking it, The old queen whispered something to her guard and with an efficient nod he disappeared back into the club.

As he was going in a statuesque blonde woman in a muscle shirt and pajama bottoms came groggily out of the same door. “What the hell Sally, why am I up?” she asked. Lucas being a typical young male looked her over and smiled. It did not go unnoticed by Sally who shook his head pityingly “No dear, wrong equipment” he said to him. “But we will find you a nice girl, never fear, sally is on the job” he said patting Lucas on the shoulder. He caught the rolling eyes from Job and suppressed a smiled. “V, I need you to check these credentials and let me know if they are clean” he said throwing the packet the guard left on the table to her. With a fumbling catch the young woman cursed and gave Sally an evil gaze. “If anyone else had asked at this time” she left the rest unfinished as the blonde returned the way she came, Lucas trying to avoid ogling her backside, but unsuccessfully. He caught Sally’s gaze “poor boy” she sighed and turned as the guard came back out with a small black square of cloth that had straps attached to it. As Sally turned it Lucas could see six of the knives strapped into one side of the black canvas cloth.

“Try this one” he said handing the bundle gently to Lucas. He put the black square in the small of his back with the blades facing out and strapped it around his midsection, adjusting the strap for comfort he moved a bit ensuring it didn’t slip and was impressed with the setup. He nodded his approval to Job as he practiced quickly removing the blades, repeating the action to ensure he knew where each of the blades were. “I’ll get you a coat and you will be good to go young man” he said. “What about getting searched?” he asked concerned. Sally just shook her head. “Technology has made us lazy, because we count on detailed sensors , they feel there is no need to actually frisk anyone, instead trusting the sensors and cameras to warn of danger” he finished. They walked back out to the front of the club and Sally walked over to another door, reaching in and rummaging around she came out with a worn black leather coat and helped Lucas into it. Checking the fit, he stepped back and admired the way it draped across his shoulders. “Perfect” he announced, walking over to the other side of the bar and pulling out two more mugs and filling them with coffee “Now we wait for V” he said and motioned to the cups. Lucas picked up his eagerly and sipped at the hot liquid. It was amazing, the best he could ever remember having, though he had been young when he last had ingested coffee, but damn he thought as he eagerly sipped at the cup.

They sat enjoying their coffee in silence for a few moments until the door banged open and a more awake V came sauntering up to Sally handing him back the package. “It’s good, not traced or tracked” she answered shooting a look and nodded at both Job and Lucas. “Thank you dear, your amazing as always” Sally said and the woman retreated into the back room, Sally slid the package to Lucas who opened it to find a passport, driver’s license and credit cards in the name of Gavin Lock, he cocked his head and looked over at Job “Really” he said wincing, “This sounds like an old gumshoe name”. Sally quietly laughed “He does have a point” and Job shot him a pointed look. “We were in a hurry and didn’t have a lot of time to choose” he said to both of them. Lucas shrugged; beggars couldn’t really be choosers. He slipped the cards into the pocket of his jeans. “Credit cards are for emergencies only my friend” he said to Lucas who nodded “Gotcha, no shopping sprees”. Job also nodded to his forearm. “The id is also set to your chip as well, so now as far as any surveillance system or government checkpoint, you are Gavin Lock” he finished.

The two left the club with assurances to Sally that they would return later for a drink. Returning to the pawn shop, Job turned the sign to open and motioned Lucas to join him in the back room. He handed him a small amount of cash “Just in case” he said nodded to him. Job drilled his young friend on the details of his task, ensuring he knew where to go and what to look for. Once he was satisfied that Lucas had memorized his tasks he reached under the counter and pulled out a black box.

Opening the box, he produced a small metallic ear bud and a watch. Lucas had seen his share of these, it was pretty much the standard electronic suite everyone carried, it was how they communicated how they got their news, it was the lifeline to their world.

Job handed him the two devices, Lucas put in the ear but and strapped on and powered the watch. With a pull motion the screen hovered above the watch as he quickly and navigated the holo ui, finding two contacts “Job” and “Sally” in the phone. With a quick wave of his hand the screen descended back into the watch. Job leveled a serious gaze at the young man “Nothing gets talked about or messaged on this device, always assume that anything said will be heard and analyzed by the government, because it will be. If there is an emergency, I will tell you to return to the store because of a toaster issue, if I message you that, stop whatever you are doing and get back here as fast as you can, got it?” he asked and Lucas solemnly nodded.

Stepping out of the door to the pawn show Lucas bundled up his coat as snow began falling lightly from the sky, the coat despite being light was surprisingly warm as he turned right and headed down I Street the snow beginning to accumulate on the ruins of townhouses that lined the cracked and broken asphalt. Lucas turned right on seventh street wrapped up in his thoughts as he approached the intersection of G street, he spied four young men who looked to be late teens or early adults, all of them wore red bandanas on their head, signifying some sort of gang. Lucas narrowed his eyes as the youths noticed him, moving to block his path. Lucas understood this all too well, he was an unknown element on their turf, there was only one way through this that would allow him to move about this area unmolested , he didn’t relish what he had to do , but he had been trained as a weapon, now was the time to use it, He thought about pulling one of the knives and then dismissed it , this would be much more effective if he did this unarmed.

As the hoods approached each looking eagerly as if they were eyeing prey come upon there hunting ground, the biggest, probably the leader stepped directly in Lucas’s path, causing him to stop short. “Nice watch” he said folding his arms over his large pecks “Hand it over, if you want to walk away”. Lucas took a steadying breath and widened his stance. Hardening his face and with as much menace as the young man could muster Lucas advanced one step, forcing the thug back two steps “You are going to want to back off, if you value walking” he said the four youths laughed “Listen to one eye here, ooooo I’m scared” said the smallest of the trio causing all of them to laugh uproariously.

The leader threw a wide haymaker Lucas stepped into it , slapping the arm down, with his right hand he latched onto the thug’s crotch with an iron grip, lifting him off the ground, the big guy let out a long wheeze as his feet left the pavement, with his left hand he quickly pushed a flat palm against his chest, causing him to fall back, as he became horizontal , Lucas let go of his crotch, the leader fell on the ground with a grunt and then withered into a fetal position, grabbing his balls. The little one, joker Lucas thought of him produced a lead pipe from behind his back and launched himself at Lucas running full speed and swinging the pipe at his head. Lucas blocked his swing by hitting his forearm with the jokers, he drove is other fist into his solar plexus and finished him by boxing his ears and driving his heel into the thugs left knee. He heard the satisfying crunch as the kneecap shattered under his foot.

The third one came at him driving punches and causing Lucas to loose ground. He drove his arms up knocking the thugs to the side, boxes his ears and then threw a four punch combo at his mid-section, Lucas took his right hand and braced it under the thugs chin pushing both up and back, taking the thug off balance and dropping him to the ground. He focused his attention on the last one, he stood there, his eyes the size of saucers as his hands shook with fear. “Boo” Lucas whispered, and the thug took off down the street. He winced as Lucas surveyed the damage he had done, he only hoped it was enough to allow him to walk around unmolested. He stepped over the groaning thugs and continued to the checkpoint.

Lucas stood in line waiting his turn as the guards processed people one at a time. Once they reached him, Lucas could see the screen come up with his picture and new name, knowing they pulled it off the chip in his arm, which continuously broadcasted his basic identification. He breathed easier once the bored guard, looked at the screen and pulled up the request for delivery. “So, you delivering for Xanadu imports, to a Mr. Johnson at the Capitol?” asked the guard, eyeing Lucas’s bag. He nodded, and did his best to seem bored, as if this was a regular thing for him. After a moment the guard waved him through, and Lucas walked from the discarded world of Poverty Town into the clean and well maintained New American capital.

Lucas walked a block and then pulled up the screen on his watch, he requested a cab and only had to wait for a short time until a golf cart sized yellow transport lowered near him. Getting in he said, “Capitol Hill” and then leaned back as the vehicle lifted to about twenty five feet, high enough to not disturb pedestrians but low enough to be out of normal traffic as cabs tended to do. The little cart weaved in and out of buildings as it made its way towards the center of DC and the four buildings that made up the infrastructure of New America. The Cart lowered itself onto the National Mall and Lucas got out, using his watch to debit Job’s account for the ride. He walked towards the capitol, watching as people walked to work, ate lunch and generally idled around the beautiful green park. As he reached near the capitol Lucas turned right and entered the Rayburn office complex, he dropped off the package at the front desk for Mr. Johnson and then walked out, trying to orient himself to his next task.

He didn’t want any record of his trip to these next two locations and decided to walk. He began walking north across the mall, as he moved over the gravel walkways, he began to casually scan the crowd, any reflective surface gave him a view behind him, he was looking for anyone that was wrong, anything out of place or anyone he saw more than once. He didn’t think anyone would tail him, or even know to tail him. But he had the process drilled into his head, anytime he went anywhere be aware of who and what was around you at all times, Dyson had drilled into him until it was second nature as normal as breathing.

Lucas left the mall and walked a block more until he stood in front of the National Archives Building. The tall columns and white stone surface gave the building a very roman look as most of the older government builds did.

The archives had been closed for nearly fifty years as all records were now digital and property of New America, only the approved history was available and anything that did not corroborate that was considered treasonous and banned from print or publication. He remembered hearing that the contents of the Archive here and the Archive II in College Park MD were no longer in the building, some vague tragic fire and computer virus having wiped most of the records away, along with the Library of Congress meant that anything printed prior to the formation of New America was gone.

When first hearing the story in school Lucas had thought nothing of it, but now, after Dyson’s stories he couldn’t imagine how anything could think that was an accident. The building was set to reopen housing some new office of the Department of Finance, but they were still in the renovation process. Lucas walked around the left side of the building as was the instructions he was given. He began walking the wall looking at the contours of the stone until he came upon what he was looking for.

Carved into a brick right above the ground level was an upside V with a picture of an envelope. “Bingo” he said and then dug into the dirt a little way uncovering a small waterproof tin. Opening it he found a folded piece of paper in it. He grabbed it up and put the paper in his pocket. Replacing the tin in the ground and covering it as best he could to hide any trace that the ground had been disturbed.

He walked back around the front of the building and then turned west heading to his next destination. Using his instincts, he circled the old Archive building once, keeping vigilant as he scanned the crowd. He was halfway back around when he crossed the street seeming to look at a suit on a mannequin in a shop window. Really, he scanned the crowd using the reflection in the mirror and there he was, He first saw him on the backside of the Archives standing reading the paper as he passed. Now that same man was looking off towards the east holding a guide map, but the map was upside down as he seemed to be concentrating on it. “Dammit” Lucas whispered; he had picked up a tail.

Lucas chose a random direction and began heading that way, keeping track of every reflection he could find to ensure that the man was still following him, at first he thought he had lost him until as he came to a corner and looked back, he could see the person turned the other way seeming to look back at the Archives. “Gotcha” he whispered to himself and then quickly crossed the street. He needed to find a private place to deal with this, he had to get rid of this tail and it couldn’t be allowed to ID him or figure out where he came from lest it lead back to Job and his shop. Lucas studied alleys and causeways until he found one with a little privacy he subtly looked back to ensure he could be seen by the guy tailing him, he casually walked into the alley once around the corner he put on a burst of speed until he came to an alcove and ducked into it. Lucas flattened himself to the wall and peeked out as his shadow turned the corner and began walking down the alley, his eyes wary and alert. The shadows pace slowed; Lucas figured he sensed the trap. Reaching up he quietly removed one of the daggers reversing the grip he recalled Dyson and his training. “When taking a person, try and maintain the element of surprise, knives are personal, they are up-close, if the assailant has a gun, run the knife deep along the inner crook of his arm, severing the tendons , this will make his gun arm useless, then stab crotch, and lunch this will incapacitate your assailant and he will be dead in moments.”. Lucas tensed for the attack listening as the footfalls approached.

Expelling the breath, he had been holding he quickly stepped out and froze. His shadow was there, unarmed and Lucas didn’t know if he could kill this man, this unarmed person who stood there afraid and now holding his hands up. He fought with himself, the logical part arguing that if he did not, he would be found out, he could be killed or thrown back in jail, that Job was in danger, and the other part telling him that this one act would change him forever, would darken his soul. The argument took a second, and in the end saving his friends won out. Lucas moved the knife lashing down on this man and just before he struck the shadow jumped back and screamed “Job sent me” he screamed, his voice cracking with fear.

Lucas jumped back, Anger replacing his warring emotions of guilt and fear. “What the hell is wrong with you, you almost fucking died” he spat at the unknown man, as he tried to gain control of his adrenaline-fueled body. He put his hands, his shaking hands in his pocket, he didn’t want the man to see them. “he told me to follow you to see if you noticed, I was to test you” he said his hands up in front of him in defense. Lucas shook his head “Put your hands down, I am not going to hurt you” he said. Lucas slipped the knife back into the sheath at the small of his back. It took a few times as his hands still quaked, both from Adrenaline and what he had almost done. “Get the hell out of here” Lucas said, and the man ran as fast as he could from the alley. Lucas put his back to the wall and slid down, trying to control his panicked breathing.

After a few moments he gained control of himself and fifteen minutes later he was able to calm down and walk from the alley. There was no sign of his tail, but he didn’t expect there would be. He turned right and reoriented himself, heading east three blocks he came to an address that was a four-story historic brick apartment building.

Walking around the building he found another symbol, here is worked a loose brick from the wall finding another note, grabbing it up he put it in his pocket.

Lucas walked another two blocks before he called a cab and had them drop him off near the checkpoint. The walk back was uneventful and when he entered the pawn shop Job was behind the counter watching videos and looking bored. Anger flashed again as he saw the older man “Your boy almost got killed” he said walking down the aisle. Job put a finger to his mouth Lucas cursed to himself, never speak around electronics. Nodding he headed upstairs while Job closed the shop for the day. When he came upstairs, he had Lucas as well as himself put the watch and earbud into the same black box he had pulled them out of. Once they were in he turned to Lucas “This is a faraday box, it grounds all signals, nothing gets in or out of the box, this is the only way we know we are save from any surveillance.” He finished and then waited expectantly for Lucas to vent. He was sure the older man could see the anger on his face and that took a little wind out of Lucas’s sails. “The guy you sent to test me, almost died” he stated, walking into the kitchen to get a drink of water, mostly just wanted to put space between himself and Job, afraid he might punch him in the face.

Job didn’t answer for a moment, walking over to Lucas and putting a hand on his shoulder. “But you didn’t, the question I have for you, if you had to, could you have?” he asked gently. Lucas remembered the internal struggle he had, the argument and then the outcome, thus part of why he was angry with himself, not Job. Nodding he turned to his friend “yes, yes I would have killed him” he finally said. Job nodded solemnly “Im sorry, I had to know, more importantly I had to let you know if you would” he looked his friend in the eye “There will come a time where you will have to , in order to protect yourself or others, you will have to take a life, I needed you to be prepared mentally and to know yourself if you were capable, training is one thing, actually doing is an entirely different thing”

Lucas lowered his eyes and nodded, he understood and put in his friends position he would have done the same, he had read enough tactical training and tactical philosophies to know the reason for it. “Did you get the notes?” Job asked changing the subject. Lucas nodded, thankful for the change and pulled the two notes. He opened them and looked at the numbers. He squinted at the page, Lucas had studied many different potential ciphers and cipher formats, but this one was either custom or incomplete. “What kind of cipher is this?” he asked Job handing him the paper. The other man just smiled “It was my idea, the problem with typical ciphers is that if they ever got ahold of one of our messages it would be Childs play for a powerful semi AI system to decrypt it, so in order to prevent that I created a book cypher that was a little more interpretive.” He said, pulling a copy of Gideon’s bible out of a drawer and opening it. “First there is a number at the top of the page, that is the month the message was written, in this case eleven for November” he said flipping the book open. “So, the month correlates to the first twelve books in the bible, in this case the book of kings, specifically The Third book of kings, now there are a series of three numbers the first is the chapter then passage then word. Job pushed the book and the note over to Lucas , he studied the numbers on the page. 
the message read 
1.9.2|6.7.16|1.2.10|7.2.22|4.26.5| 7.28.16|4.12.8|7.10.11|8.40.8

It took Lucas a few moments as he flipped back and forth within the old book, finally smiling he read the note to Job “Adonias ready for fifty thousand gold Thanac drop ten days” then he looked curiously at his friend “Thanac, Adonias?” Job smiled at the younger man. “Adonias is the code name for a high level contact we are paying to sway a vote within the Department of Security to prevent putting up cameras in the poverty bloc, Thanac drop is the archive drop” he finished. Lucas nodded and then went to work on the next message, once he was done, he looked oddly at Job reading the ominous note “Judas in our midst, danger close, meet last supper tomorrow eve” he said confused. Job’s expression turned troubled. This is not good but looks like we are going to dinner tomorrow night.
